issues.legal_issue: A statutory cutoff limiting relief by reopening closed transactions does not necessarily prevent a special court from granting redemption relief concerning an earlier transaction.
material_facts: The suit sought redemption and possession of property subject to mortgages made before the statutory cutoff.
The claim did not require reopening a closed transaction.
issues.conclusion: The special court had jurisdiction to entertain the redemption suit despite the age of the mortgage transactions.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Sangli State Agriculturists Protection Act, 1936, the cutoff limited relief by way of reopening closed transactions; it did not bar other relief, including redemption, concerning earlier transactions. The Act contained no express general restriction on the court's jurisdiction over such transactions.

predicates.special_debt_relief_proceeding: The claim is brought in a special proceeding created to grant relief from indebtedness.
predicates.transaction_predates_relief_cutoff: The transaction at issue occurred before the cutoff for reopening closed transactions.
predicates.relief_is_redemption_not_reopening: The relief sought is redemption rather than reopening a closed transaction.

issues.definition: When an earlier transaction is involved in a special debt-relief proceeding seeking redemption rather than reopening, the special court may entertain the claim.

issues.legal_issue: A successor who was not represented in execution proceedings and whose status as legal representative was not adjudicated need not set aside an execution sale to assert an unaffected inheritance.
material_facts: A money decree was executed against the deceased predecessor, but a brother was substituted without any dispute or adjudication about who was the true legal representative.
The property was sold in execution, and the successor asserting inheritance had not been made a party to the execution proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The successor was entitled to ignore the execution sale, and the suit was not barred under Article 12 of the Limitation Act.
issues.legal_principle: Article 12 of the Limitation Act did not bar the claim because the successor was not affected by the sale and need not sue to set it aside. The Court distinguished Malkarjun Bin Shidramappa Pasare v. Narhari Bin Shivappa, (1900) L.R. 27 I.A. 216, where the executing court had adjudicated who was the legal representative; the Court doubted that decision but held it distinguishable on the facts.

predicates.inheritance_claim_proceeding: The proceeding asserts a right inherited from a deceased predecessor.
predicates.execution_sale_followed_substitution_wit: An execution sale followed substitution of a person as legal representative without judicial determination of a dispute over that person's status.
predicates.successor_not_party_to_execution: The successor asserting the inherited right was not a party to the execution proceedings.

issues.definition: A successor asserting an inherited right may ignore an execution sale when the successor was not a party and the substituted representative's status was not adjudicated.

issues.legal_issue: The shorter limitation period for possession after a mortgagee's transfer applies only when the defendant affirmatively proves that the transfer exceeded the mortgagee's interest.
material_facts: The suit sought possession after redemption of mortgaged property.
The defendants relied on transfers by the mortgagee or successors to invoke the shorter limitation period.
The transfer documents were not produced, and the defendants did not affirmatively establish that a transfer conveyed a larger interest than the mortgage allowed.
issues.conclusion: Article 134 did not apply; Article 148 was the applicable limitation provision, and the suit was within time.
issues.legal_principle: Under Articles 134 and 148 of the Limitation Act, Article 134 required affirmative proof that the mortgagee or successor transferred a larger interest than the mortgage justified; absent that proof, the longer limitation period under Article 148 applied. The Court did not decide the separate dispute about who had to prove the date of the plaintiff's knowledge of the transfer.

predicates.redemption_possession_suit: The proceeding seeks possession of property after redemption of a mortgage.
predicates.mortgagee_excess_transfer_proven: The defendant has affirmatively proved that the mortgagee or successor transferred an interest greater than the mortgage justified.

issues.definition: In a possession suit after redemption, the longer mortgage limitation applies if the defendant has not proved that the mortgagee's transfer exceeded the mortgage interest.

issues.legal_issue: A suit for redemption is not incompetent merely because heirs of a deceased defendant are absent when they have no subsisting interest or are not shown to be jointly interested in the property in suit.
material_facts: One deceased defendant had remained ex parte, and the record indicated that he had no subsisting interest in the mortgaged property.

Some representatives of another deceased defendant had been substituted but were not served; the record did not establish that they were jointly interested in the property with those already before the court.
issues.conclusion: The preliminary objections did not make the suit as a whole incompetent; any determination would not bind the absent heirs of the defendant who had no subsisting interest.
issues.legal_principle: Order 34, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires persons interested in the mortgage security or right of redemption to be joined. The Court held that the suit was not defeated where the absent heirs had no subsisting interest or were not shown to be necessary jointly interested parties. It also held that failure to serve some substituted representatives did not itself establish abatement under Order 22, rule 4.

predicates.redemption_suit: The proceeding seeks redemption of mortgaged property.
predicates.absent_heirs_of_deceased_party: Heirs of a deceased defendant are not before the court.
predicates.deceased_party_had_no_subsisting_interes: The deceased defendant had no subsisting interest in the property in suit.
predicates.absent_heirs_not_shown_jointly_intereste: The record does not show that the absent heirs are jointly interested in the property with the parties before the court.

issues.definition: A redemption suit is not incompetent for absence of a deceased defendant's heirs when the deceased had no subsisting interest or the heirs are not shown to be jointly interested.

issues.legal_issue: A document recording severance of joint status without allotting specific property by metes and bounds is not compulsorily registrable and may be admitted to prove that severance.
material_facts: Documents recorded a separation among members of a Mitakshara coparcenary and were used to show that they became separate in estate.
The documents were not relied on to prove a partition by allotment of specific properties by metes and bounds.
issues.conclusion: The documents were admissible for the limited purpose of proving severance of joint status, despite being unregistered.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 17(1)(b) of the Registration Act, a written partition by specific allotment of properties is compulsorily registrable. A partition consisting only of severance of joint status and definition of shares, without specific allotments, does not affect rights in immovable property in the manner contemplated by that provision and is not barred from evidence by section 49. The Court applied the distinction between the two forms of partition under Mitakshara law.

rule.if: document_offered_as_partition_evidence and mitakshara_coparcenary and document_records_status_severance and not document_allots_specific_property

predicates.document_offered_as_partition_evidence: A document is offered as evidence of a partition among family members.
predicates.mitakshara_coparcenary: The family members are governed by the Mitakshara law of coparcenary.
predicates.document_records_status_severance: The document records that a member's joint status has been severed and shares defined.
predicates.document_allots_specific_property: The document allots specific properties to individual members by metes and bounds.

issues.definition: A document offered to prove severance in a Mitakshara coparcenary is admissible for that purpose if it does not allot specific property.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant who inherits one co-owner's share in property mortgaged in its entirety may recover only that inherited share when another co-owner's share has passed to another person.
material_facts: The family documents established separation in estate but did not establish a partition by specific allotment of the mortgaged properties.
The mortgages covered the entire ancestral property, although the borrowing was by one brother and the others acted as sureties.
After the death of another brother and the mother, the claimant's father and his surviving brother held equal shares; the surviving brother's share was transferred to the mortgagee's son.
issues.conclusion: The claimant's decree for possession after redemption was confined to the half share inherited from her father, and the appeal was allowed to the extent of the other half share.
issues.legal_principle: Under Mitakshara law, severance of joint status without allotment of specific properties leaves the separated members with defined shares in the property. Because the mortgages covered the entire property, the claimant could recover only the share inherited from her father, not the other co-owner's share that had been transferred.

rule.if: redemption_claim_by_heir and coowners_severed_in_status_without_specific_allotment and mortgage_covers_entire_property and claimant_inherited_only_one_coowner_share

predicates.redemption_claim_by_heir: An heir seeks possession after redemption of mortgaged property.
predicates.coowners_severed_in_status_without_speci: The co-owners became separate in status but did not divide the property into specific allotments.
predicates.mortgage_covers_entire_property: The mortgage encumbers the entire property held by the co-owners.
predicates.claimant_inherited_only_one_coowner_shar: The claimant inherited the share of one co-owner but did not inherit the other co-owner's share.

issues.definition: An heir's recovery after redemption is limited to the share inherited when the mortgage covers the whole property but the heir succeeds to only one co-owner's share.
